value.definition: an address naming a page by a value unique among the pages sharing a property value

invariants.statement: This kind answers the unique kind `page-property`.
The index answers this kind under the page type and then the scope.
A scope is the scope property's name followed by the scope property's value.
The scope is the value the property a declaration's `uniqueProperty` names has.
That property is declared on the same page type.
That property is required and has one value.
A scope is any kind of page property rather than a relation alone.
A page has one address of this kind.

value.definition: an address naming a page by a value unique among the pages of its type

invariants.statement: This kind answers the unique kind `page-type`.
The index answers this kind under the page type named.
An address of this kind names the property the value is read by.
A page type with more than one such property is why the property is named.

value.definition: an address naming a page by a value unique across every page

invariants.statement: This kind answers the unique kind `page`.
An address of this kind names the property the value is read by.
An address of this kind names no page type.
